messages:
maya: FYI support ticket redwood-7893 - multiple customers reporting higher p95/p99 this morning, mainly on text-generation routes. Dashboard shows p95 ~800ms (was ~220ms) and p99 spikes up to 2.1s. Filing here to coordinate triage.

jon: saw the alert. I pulled traces for a few of the slow requests. They all hit the runtime for the same model family and show a big stall in the KV prefix cache layer. kv_get_latency jumps from ~2ms to ~120ms on the slow tails.

elin: I can confirm. query: rate(prefix_cache_miss_total[10m]) shows a big uptick starting ~08:12 UTC. Miss rate went from ~8% to ~65% across serving nodes in us-east-1.

samira: any recent deploys? Could be a rollout changed cache key composition or eviction behavior.

maya: We rolled the new batching/kv-ttl experiment last night (canary -> 20% traffic). The canary metric had looked fine but rollout hit 100% at 03:00 UTC.

jon: that matches timing. I'm seeing a lot of eviction logs on runtime nodes: ``evicting prefix key=<hex> mem_watermark=0.82 reason=LRU`` and then immediate gets for the same prefix from other concurrent requests -> thrash.

alex_support: customers included a couple high-cardinality prompt workloads (large number of unique prefixes). They started hitting us heavily this morning. They say nothing changed on their side.

elin: hypothesis: a combination of (1) increased prefix cardinality from those customers, (2) reduced cache residency due to smaller TTL/size change in the new config, (3) LRU causing frequent evictions -> cold misses -> p95/p99 regressions. Also saw an oddity where cache_key collisions are low but many keys are very short-lived.

jon: found what looks like a cache key bug in the rollout config: the new key includes the raw prompt string snippet without normalization, while previous code normalized whitespace and truncated long prefix tokens. That increases key variance massively. Repro attached below.

maya: can you paste the snippet?

jon: ```
// in kv_cache_key.go (canary)
key := fmt.Sprintf("%s:%s", tenantID, prefixSnippet) // missing normalization/trim
// old behavior:
// key := fmt.Sprintf("%s:%s", tenantID, normalize(prefixSnippet))
```

samira: oh oof. That explains it. If every slightly different whitespace produces a new key clients that do token-level editing will explode cardinality.

alex_support: reproduction steps from my end: curl -H 'Authorization: Bearer <key>' -d '{"prompt":"calc 1"}' https://api.redwood.example/v1/generate run N=2000 with small variations in spacing -> observe prefix_cache_miss_total jump.

elin: I ran a synthetic load: wrk -t8 -c200 -d60s against /generate with a mix of 1k unique small prefixes; results: p95 860ms, p99 2.05s. Flip config to old key normalization, restart cache process -> p95 drops to 240ms within 30s.

maya: mitigation plan (short term):
- rollback key change on canary immediately (if safe) OR
- temporarily increase cache size + bump TTL to reduce evictions
- enable per-tenant warmup for top offending tenants
- throttle offending tenants if necessary
- instrument a hotfix for normalization as high-priority

elin: I can prepare a hotfix PR for the normalization and unit tests. It's small. But we should be careful: normalizing may change existing keys and cause an initial large warmup. That's OK because normalized keys reduce long-term cardinality.

jon: for immediate relief I pushed a config change to the dedicated nodes to increase prefix_cache_max_entries from 200k -> 500k and prefix_cache_ttl from 30s -> 120s for us-east-1. Observed miss-rate fall from 65% -> 18% over 3 minutes and p95 down to ~260ms.

maya: nice. Does that require node restarts?

jon: config change applied via runtime dynamic flags, no restarts. But keep in mind memory usage jumped ~12% on nodes. We're watching memory OOMs.

samira: if memory looks marginal, might instead change eviction policy to CLOCK (less churn than strict LRU) and enable a small admission filter for very low-frequency keys. That would limit thrash without doubling memory.

elin: good idea. Also we can add a short-lived bloom filter (or TinyLFU heuristic) at admission to avoid caching one-off random prefixes. I'll prototype a quick admission filter patch.

alex_support: customers are asking for updates. We should respond: "we identified a regresssion in a cache key change deployed earlier; we've applied mitigations and are rolling a fix. We'll follow up with a postmortem." Can someone draft a short note?

maya: I'll send a templated reply and add timeline. Please put concrete numbers: p95 improved from 800ms -> 260ms after config bump; p99 down from 2.1s -> 420ms for observed set.

jon: adding PromQL queries I used for triage so support/eng can rerun quickly:
- prefix miss rate: ``sum(rate(prefix_cache_miss_total[5m])) / sum(rate(prefix_cache_req_total[5m]))``
- eviction rate: ``sum(rate(prefix_cache_evictions_total[5m]))``
- mem pressure: ``node_memory_MemAvailable_bytes / node_memory_MemTotal_bytes``

Also trace filter to find slow spans: ``trace.service=runtime and trace.span=\"kv.get\" and duration>50ms``

samira: logging suggestion: emit normalized_prefix_length and admission_result in cache debug logs (sampled) so we can detect pathological key lengths and failed admissions without enabling full debug.

elin: PR created: github.com/redwood/rt/commit/abcd1234 - adds normalizePrefix() + tests. I'll tag for emergency review.

maya: who can review now? jon?

jon: I can review and sign off in 15-20m. Once merged we can roll to canary 5% and watch prefix miss metric.

alex_support: customer SLAs - one enterprise asked for ETA for full fix. Recommend we: (1) share current mitigations (config bump), (2) say hotfix PR will be in canary within 1 hour, (3) full rollout after canary validation in ~2-3 hours assuming no regressions.

maya: agree. Also add a note to oncall runbook to rollback config or enable tenant throttle if memory climbs above 92%.

sre-bot: incident created INC-2026-115 kv-prefix-cache-thrash-us-east-1. Pager escalations disabled for the runbooks.

jon: follow-ups: (1) patch to normalize keys -> PR (elin), (2) prototype admission filter (samira) -> bench, (3) consider eviction policy change to CLOCK in next maintenance window (infra planning), (4) add per-tenant warmup for top-k prefixes (product discussion).

samira: I'll start a micro-benchmark for CLOCK vs LRU with our realistic trace generator and post results here.

maya: great work. Once we have PR merged and canary metrics show miss rate back to baseline, I'll close the support tickets and draft the postmortem. Thanks everyone. :thumbsup:
